newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says US, EU bar $4.5 bln in ag exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says US, EU bar $4.5 bln in ag exports.

text.p: Trade barriers in the United States and Europe cost Brazil $4.5 billion a year in lost agricultural exports while imports have risen to 15.5 percent of consumer goods in the Brazilian market, local newspapers said.
Jornal do Brasil, citing a Foreign Ministry report, said some 40 Brazilian products, from orange juice and shrimp to novels, are unfairly discriminated against by the U.S. and the European Union.
Meanwhile, imports, as a percentage of industrial products consumed in Brazil, rose to 15.5 percent last year from 6.3 market in 1990, according to O Estado de S. Paulo.
The paper, quoting a government-linked study by two economists, said preliminary 1996 figures show the figure has continued rising.

Brazil's Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia plans to make the case for a further opening of U.S., European and Japanese markets to Brazilian products on Monday at a World Trade Organization conference in Singapore, papers said.
A sharp hike in Brazil's trade deficit to $1.31 billion in October has raised concerns among analysts and economists about the state of the country's external accounts.
The annual trade gap is expected to reach roughly $4.7 billion this year BRAAN, compared with a $3.15 billion deficit last year.
